P. 0. Box 505

4. Glenwood Springs, CO 81601

January 31, 1973
305
The Monorable Floyd Haskell The United States Senate Washington, DC 20510
Dear Sir:
This correspondence is for the purpose of registering my indignation and opposition concerning the implementation of Executive Order 11644. This order is apparently the result of pressures from various hysterical groups such as the Sierra Club and the hippies, if there's a difference.
Following are a few reasons which I feel justify my attitude toward the subject.
Contrary to the opening wording of the order, I feel that indirectly it says that, "By virtue of the power vested in me as President of the United States, I hereby revoke your constitutional right to life, liberty, and the pursuit of happiness."
The immediate result of this order has been to create a profusion of puppet dictators in the guise of land administrators.
Here in Colorado West, the authoritative agencies have installed large signs advising one to restrict travel to constructed roads only, under threat of monetary and penal consequences. They then post many constructed roads "off limits."
It can be assumed that this regulation has been imposed as a result of erroneous reports of excessive terrain or ecological damage. In my opinion, the majority of the complainants probably can't even define the word "ecology." Regrettably, you are probably not in a position to see and establish the truth in fact for yourself.
I have no quarrel with skiers or skiing and cannot speak for the rest of the country; however, I sincerely believe that the claimed vehicular damage in Colorado West, if laid end to end, would not equal the 27 miles by 60 feet of timber and vegetation eliminated for ski trails on public lands involved in just one small complex near here.
Statistically, there are roughly We to 5 million skiers and approximately 5 million four-wheel drive vehicles averaging three occupants each. This obviously affects 15 million public land users in contrast and indicates recreational group discrimination.
